subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: When a Codex turn submission is accepted but turn start is not observed before a bounded deadline, should OpenClaw retry on a fresh thread only with explicit idempotency proof, or fail the user-visible send and require an explicit retry?
rationale: The app-server contract separates immediate turn submission from actual execution, and retrying an ambiguous request without an idempotency rule could duplicate work or messages.

options.title: Fail visibly, then retry explicitly
options.body: Treat a missing turn-start event as a failed send with a clear recovery action, avoiding an automatic duplicate turn.

options.title: Retry with durable idempotency
options.body: Automatically rotate and retry only after the gateway can prove that the original message cannot execute or can be deduplicated.

recommendation.title: Fail visibly, then retry explicitly
recommendation.body: Treat a missing turn-start event as a failed send with a clear recovery action, avoiding an automatic duplicate turn.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the closest current native-thread overflow and startup-rotation boundary.
